Eight ads, eight arguments

Every ad below is built from one locked vial shot, so the product is identical in all eight. What changes between them is not the background. It is the argument each one makes.

The locked master

One vial, generated once

This shot is generated a single time and passed into every ad as a reference. That is why the cap, the crimp, the compass mark and the label are identical in all eight rather than being redrawn each time and drifting.

The compound area is deliberately blank. No compound name, no dosage, no code. A label that names nothing makes no product claim, and one master then serves every compound instead of locking a separate vial per SKU.

Blank compound area Research use only Matte white, not holographic

The set

Diversity here is an argument count, not a layout count. Four layouts of one argument is one ad. Each card names the argument it makes and how the vial is treated to make it.

What was checked before these ran

  • Promo code is printed exactly as given. Summer30, not upper-cased. A code is a literal, and an all-caps version is not the code.
  • No imagery implying use in a person. No bodies, no hands on the vial, no needles or administration icons, no clinical treatment setting. Icons count. Checked by looking at every image, not by scanning text.
  • Purity wording sits at or below what Axion already publishes on their own storefront. Nothing was asserted on their behalf.
  • No invented compound names, dosages or codes anywhere in the set.

One art direction in the library was built around a hand holding a vial. That breaks the no-bodies rule for this category, and it would have passed every text check. It is now blocked at the source and cannot be picked for any client.
